facts.raw_span: persistent severe pain on the left side of her face
episodic sharp, electric-shock–like pain initially affecting the entire left hemiface
pain localized to the V2 and V3 distributions of the left trigeminal nerve
attacks lasted 4–5 seconds
were triggered by jaw movement during eating or tooth brushing
reached 10/10 on a numeric pain scale
allodynia to cold air
hypersensitivity to touch in the affected area
distorted sensations in the V2 region
sensory testing was otherwise normal
no other neurological deficits
Contrast-enhanced MRI of the head showed no abnormalities

concepts.why: The patient's symptoms of episodic sharp, electric-shock–like pain in the V2 and V3 distributions of the left trigeminal nerve, triggered by jaw movement, are consistent with Trigeminal Neuralgia.
The patient's recent COVID-19 vaccine administration and subsequent development of trigeminal neuralgia-like symptoms suggest a possible post-vaccine complication.
The patient's persistent severe pain on the left side of her face, with allodynia to cold air and hypersensitivity to touch, could be indicative of atypical facial pain.
Although less likely, the patient's symptoms could be related to multiple sclerosis, which can cause trigeminal neuralgia.
The patient's symptoms of facial pain and distorted sensations could also be indicative of glossopharyngeal neuralgia, although it is less likely.
The patient's symptoms of persistent severe pain on the left side of her face could also be indicative of occipital neuralgia.
The patient's symptoms of facial pain, triggered by jaw movement, could be related to a temporomandibular joint disorder.
The patient's symptoms of persistent severe pain on the left side of her face, without a clear cause, could be indicative of persistent idiopathic facial pain.

It explains the episodic sharp, electric-shock–like pain affecting the V2 and V3 distributions of the left trigeminal nerve, despite normal sensory testing and no abnormalities on contrast-enhanced MRI of the head.
